one_line_contribution: An ALFWorld text wrapper that plants per-kitchen appliance-name bindings (which of two identical-looking receptacles heats/cools/cleans) and crosses them with whether a wrong choice is detectable from feedback, to show that a per-instance lookup - scene-keyed retrieval or a reader-routed compiled table - beats a 60-token run-time-probe instruction only in the regime where the environment returns no signal.
closest_prior_work: The strongest verified threats are partial, not pre-emptive. 2606.22936 'When Agents Commit Too Soon' (verified via s2cli paper; S2 channel) already frames silent, unrecoverable commitment as the failure mode the untestable regime instantiates, but it is a hidden-state diagnostic and manipulates neither testability nor the memory form. 2605.22219 SGR-Bench (verified) already establishes that agents fail by not establishing the correct site-specific state, i.e. the 'binding' half of this proposal, without any static-vs-retrieved contrast. The sharpest threat to the *informativeness* of P1/P3 is 2607.10608 'The Compliance Trap: Diagnosing How AI Agents Consume Conflicting Memory' (returned by my recent-restricted mechanism search on the HF channel; I did not run a `paper` verification on it, so treat the ID as search-returned rather than individually verified), which already reports that readers adopt conflicting retrieved memory early and compound on it - i.e. that a retrieved name overrides a prior is closer to known than the proposal's P1/P3 framing admits. 2608.26730 'Knowing When Not to Reuse: Conditional Experience Transfer' (verified) is the nearest thing to the probe-before-reuse idea, but it authorizes reuse with bounded trials before *weight-changing training*, not at inference, so it does not pre-empt. None of these plants bindings, manipulates feedback testability, or runs rule/table/retrieval arms on the same games. The prior the proposal cannot search away is structural rather than bibliographic: 'you need stored information exactly for the latent state you cannot observe' is the textbook POMDP observability statement, and a skeptical AC will read the headline as an empirical restatement of it.
strongest_objection: The central 'only when untestable' interaction is manufactured by the wrapper rather than discovered, and the proposal's own P4 contradicts its title. Three parts. (a) The rule half of the interaction is definitional and the proposal says so: under untestable the probe rule 'is inert by construction', and D(S1, untestable) is filed as a construction check, not a prediction. What remains under testable is a compliance measurement - does a 32B reader execute a two-branch instruction when the environment tells it the branch fired - which is a fact about the reader, not about when experience memory needs a query. (b) P4 predicts that a compiled ~30-row table (a static, cached, once-compiled artifact) removes the untestable penalty as fully as retrieval does. If that holds, a query is *never* necessary in this study, in either regime; the surviving claim is 'a per-instance lookup is necessary', where 'lookup' includes a prompt, which is compile_dont_retrieve (archived 6.0) restated with a manipulation attached rather than overturned. The retrieval-vs-table distinction is then routing mechanism (reader-routed signature vs embedding-routed key), not memory necessity, and the title overclaims relative to what the plan can return. (c) Necessity is preserved only by excluding the obvious binding-free workaround: the proposal itself names a ~30-token redundancy rule ('do the step at both appliances') that would remove the untestable penalty with no memory at all, and rules it out by making the untestable regime irreversible by authorial choice - the failed step is silently spent, later attempts are no-ops. Irreversibility is a property of the wrapper, not of ALFWorld or of real silent-API settings, so the 'query is necessary' half is engineered. Secondary but concrete: the manipulation is a lexical-prior fight (calling a stoveburner 'microwave'), so P1/P3 measure knowledge-conflict override under adversarial renaming rather than acquisition of an arbitrary instance binding, and the result will not transfer to bindings the model has no prior about. And the untestable regime's leak probe covers only non-procedure actions across swap states; it does not verify that post-procedure state inspection (examine the object after the fake success string) fails to reveal the silent failure - if it does reveal it, the untestable regime is probe-able after all and P3 measures something else.
what_would_fix_it: Four changes, in order of importance. (1) Drop the 'query' framing the plan cannot support and pre-register the honest headline: which *artifact* form carries an unobservable instance binding - reader-routed table vs scene-keyed retrieval vs oracle - with the query-necessity claim retired unless S2 fails. (2) Run the redundancy rule as a first-class arm under untestable (the 30-token 'do the step at both appliances' instruction), and add the third regime the proposal excludes (undetectable but reversible). If a binding-free redundancy rule matches retrieval, that is the paper's real and more interesting result; suppressing the arm makes the necessity claim unfalsifiable. (3) Add a neutral-name binding level (appliance_a / appliance_b, or novel tokens) alongside the microwave/stoveburner swap, so prior-override and binding-acquisition are separated; report the interaction of binding lexicality with regime. Without it a reviewer reads the whole study as a knowledge-conflict experiment. (4) Fix the statistics the entailment check already flagged: delete the TOST conjuncts in P2 and P4 (each is implied by its own first conjunct plus the near-zero floor on D, which violates the brief's no-prediction-entailed-by-a-definition rule), define the 12-20 band left open in P1, re-specify W- so it carries a known-wrong binding rather than the correct one half the time, and extend the leak probe to post-procedure state inspection under untestable.
missing_baseline: Two. Primary: the binding-free redundancy rule under untestable - a ~30-token 'perform the procedure step at both candidate appliances' instruction on the static3 base. The proposal names it and excludes it by declaring the untestable regime irreversible; a reviewer will demand it, because it is the cheapest artifact that could remove the untestable penalty with no bank, no table and no query, and its success would falsify the headline without touching any of P1-P6. Secondary: k0 (no-memory) at q = .5 under both regimes. It is cut on the assertion that 'a stale prior is the same floor as a stale exemplar', but S0's exemplars actively name the wrong appliance, so the swap penalty of a memory-free reader is the correct reference for deciding whether the penalty is caused by the stale artifact or by the model's lexical prior - exactly the attribution the paper needs for P1 and P3.

Judgment of the proposal's own check: it is above average for this round - five queries with declared classes, channels and returned IDs, including a genuine home-vocabulary query stripped of agent/memory words, and every ID I sampled from it resolves. Two weaknesses. First, its Q9 concludes that no AWM variant has a run-time probe, but it states in the same sentence that AWM itself was not returned; my repeat of that query also failed to return AWM, so the claim about the closest named method rests on a search that never located the method - an absent search reported as clearance. Second, all queries are aimed at the agent-memory framing; none is aimed at the knowledge-conflict / context-vs-parametric-prior literature (compliance trap, memory conflict, entity substitution), which is where P1 and P3 actually live and where the outcome is closest to already known.
